description: Shell Interop (!cmd) - Add ability to run external commands from JACL. !cmd returns stdout as lazy stream, error value on failure. [exec ...] returns full struct. Supports Jobs (&), OS pipes, stdin from streams, sandboxing via prelude.

userStories.title: Lexer recognizes `!` prefix
userStories.description: As the lexer, I need to recognize `!` at the start of a command as the external command prefix.
acceptanceCriteria: `!` at command position produces TOKEN_BANG or similar
`!ls` lexes as bang + identifier `ls`
`!git status` lexes as bang + identifier `git` + identifier `status`
`!!` (bang-bang for last command) is NOT in scope — just single `!`
Existing `!` usage (if any) doesn't break
Lexer tests added
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Lexer already had TOKEN_BANG support. Added 8 tests verifying shell interop syntax.

userStories.title: Parser handles `!cmd` syntax
userStories.description: As the parser, I need to parse `!cmd args...` and produce an AST node that the compiler can process.
acceptanceCriteria: `!ls -la` parses to AST node with command="ls", args=["-la"]
`!git status --short` parses correctly with multiple args
`!"my script.sh"` works (quoted command name)
`!$cmd` works (variable as command name)
`!cmd ..$args` works (splat for args)
Parse errors for malformed `!` usage produce clear messages
Parser tests added
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added AST_SHELL_CMD node type with head/args structure. Shell commands stop at pipe/and/or/amp but not general operators like -. 10 parser tests added.

userStories.title: Compiler emits code for `!cmd`
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to transform `!cmd args...` into bytecode that will spawn a process.
acceptanceCriteria: `!ls -la` compiles to OP_EXEC or equivalent with args
`!$cmd $arg1 $arg2` compiles with variable references preserved
`!cmd ..$args` compiles with splat preserved
Compiler checks that `exec` is available in the prelude/env
If `exec` is not in prelude (sandboxed), compile error: "exec not available"
Compiler tests added
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added AST_SHELL_CMD handling to compiler__compile_node and all analysis functions. Shell commands transform to [exec head args...] calls. 6 compiler tests added.

userStories.title: `!cmd` returns stdout stream
userStories.description: As the VM, I need `!cmd` to spawn a child process and return stdout as a lazy stream.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_EXEC opcode (or similar) added to bytecode
`exec` capability added to default prelude (via [interpret-prelude])
`!ls` runs `ls` and returns stdout as a stream
`!ls -la /tmp` passes multiple args correctly
Child process inherits parent's environment variables
Child process inherits parent's working directory
Stream is lazy — large outputs don't buffer fully in memory
`{!echo "hello" | collect}` returns `"hello\n"` (string after collect)
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added OP_EXEC opcode and STREAM_KIND_EXEC. Compiler emits OP_VEC + OP_EXEC directly for shell commands. VM spawns process via popen, returns lazy stdout stream. Collect on exec streams returns full output. 5 integration tests added.

userStories.title: `!cmd` error handling — exit codes
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want failed commands to return error values so pipes short-circuit correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Exit code 0: return stdout stream
Exit code non-zero: return JACL error value
Error value's message is stderr content (lossy UTF-8)
`!false` returns error value (exit 1)
`{!sh -c "echo err >&2; exit 1"}` error message contains "err"
Error composes with pipes: `{!false | for x { print $x }}` — for never runs
Error works with catch: `{!false | catch {"fallback"}}`
Integration tests for error cases
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Exit code 0 returns stdout stream. Non-zero exit returns JACL error value with stderr content. Error propagates through stream for loops via OP_JUMP_IF_ERROR. Error works with try/catch. 6 integration tests added.

userStories.title: `[exec ...]` full form — struct result
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want access to stdout, stderr, and exit code separately for cases where I need full control.
acceptanceCriteria: `[exec "cmd" args...]` returns struct `{stream stdout, str stderr, i32 exit}`
Struct fields accessible via `->`: `$result->stdout`, `$result->exit`
`$result->stdout` is a stream (same as `!cmd` on success)
`$result->stderr` is a string (lossy UTF-8)
Works even when exit is non-zero (doesn't return error value)
Integration test: capture both stdout and stderr from a command
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added OP_EXEC_FULL opcode. [exec ...] returns map with {stdout, stderr, exit}. stdout is STREAM_KIND_EXEC_BUFFER (yields lines, collects to string). 6 integration tests added.

userStories.title: Stdin from JACL strings
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to pipe JACL strings into external commands as stdin.
acceptanceCriteria: `{"hello world" | !wc -w}` feeds string to wc's stdin
Pipe detected at compile time or runtime — string goes to stdin, not arg
Works with multi-line strings
Works with string variables: `{$data | !grep "pattern"}`

Integration test: `{"a
b
c" | !wc -l | collect}` returns "3
"
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added OP_EXEC_STDIN opcode. compiler__compile_pipe_op detects AST_SHELL_CMD RHS and emits stdin-piped exec. String stdin written to temp file, passed via shell redirection. 5 integration tests added. Note: -flag style args are split by lexer into separate tokens; tests use commands that don't require flags (cat, grep with pattern).

userStories.title: Stdin from JACL streams
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to pipe JACL streams into external commands lazily.
acceptanceCriteria: Stream piped to `!cmd` feeds elements to stdin incrementally
`{[lines "a\nb\nc"] | !cat}` works (stream to external)
Large streams don't materialize fully in memory
Works with `{!cmd1 | !cmd2}` (external stream to external)
Integration test with stream input
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Extended OP_EXEC_STDIN to handle streams via vm__pull_stream_one(). Elements collected incrementally with auto newline insertion. Error propagation from upstream commands (e.g., !false | !cat) handled. 5 integration tests added. Note: stream elements are collected to memory before exec (true OS pipes deferred to US-009).

userStories.title: OS pipes between adjacent external commands
userStories.description: As the runtime, I want adjacent `!cmd | !cmd` to use real OS pipes for efficiency.
acceptanceCriteria: `{!ls | !grep ".txt"}` creates OS pipe (stdout of ls → stdin of grep)
No intermediate JACL stream materialization for adjacent externals
`{!cmd1 | !cmd2 | !cmd3}` chains multiple OS pipes
Mixed pipes work: `{!ls | filter [\\ match-re $it ".txt"] | !sort}` — ls output goes through JACL filter, then to sort
Compiler/runtime detects adjacent external commands for optimization
Integration test: large data through `{!cat file | !head -1}` doesn't OOM
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added OP_EXEC_PIPE opcode and STREAM_KIND_EXEC_PIPE. Compiler detects adjacent shell command chains and emits OP_EXEC_PIPE. VM uses fork()/pipe()/dup2()/execvp() to create true Unix pipelines. Last command exit code determines pipeline success. 3 integration tests added.

userStories.title: Jobs — background execution with `&`
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to run external commands in the background and interact with the process.
acceptanceCriteria: `!cmd &` syntax parses and compiles
Returns a `Job` value (a Future that wraps an OS process)
`await $job` returns the ExecResult struct `{stdout, stderr, exit}`
`$job->pid` returns the OS process ID
Job doesn't block — parent continues immediately
Integration test: start background process, do other work, await result
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added background field to AST shell_cmd, TOKEN_AMP parsing for & suffix. Added OP_EXEC_BG opcode. VM forks and returns Job map {pid, _is_job, _stdout_path, _stderr_path}. OP_AWAIT_SM detects Job maps and does blocking waitpid, returns ExecResult {stdout, stderr, exit}. 4 integration tests added.

userStories.title: Jobs — signals and cancellation
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to send signals to background processes.
acceptanceCriteria: `[signal $job SIGTERM]` sends signal to the process, returns `$true`
`[signal $job SIGKILL]` works
`[cancel $job]` kills the process (sends SIGTERM)
Signal on completed job returns `$false` (no error, no-op)
Integration test: start long-running process, cancel it, verify it stopped
Integration test: signal completed job, verify returns `$false`
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added OP_SIGNAL and OP_CANCEL opcodes. [signal $job SIGNAME] supports SIGTERM, SIGKILL, SIGINT, SIGHUP, SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2. [cancel $job] is shorthand for SIGTERM. Returns $true on success, $false if process already exited. 5 integration tests added.

userStories.title: REPL `$PATH` fallback
userStories.description: As a REPL user, I want bare unknown commands to fall back to `$PATH` lookup so I can use the REPL as a shell.
acceptanceCriteria: In REPL mode: `ls -la` (without `!`) tries `$PATH` lookup if `ls` is not a JACL binding
In script mode: `ls -la` is a compile error (no implicit fallback)
Fallback only triggers for command position, not expressions
User can disable fallback in REPL via setting/pragma
Integration test for REPL fallback behavior
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Added shell_fallback flag to Compiler. Prelude key :shell-fallback enables REPL shell fallback. When enabled and exec is available, unknown commands in command position are executed via OP_EXEC. 6 integration tests added.

userStories.title: Sandboxing — `exec` as prelude entry
userStories.description: As the sandboxing system, I need `exec` to be a prelude-controlled capability.
acceptanceCriteria: `exec` is in the default prelude returned by `[interpret-prelude]`
`[interpret {} "!ls"]` fails with compile error (exec not available)
`[interpret [interpret-prelude] "!ls"]` works
`[interpret [map-remove [interpret-prelude] "exec"] "!ls"]` fails
Custom exec can be injected: `[interpret {"exec": $my-exec} "!ls"]`
Jobs (`&`) also blocked when exec is unavailable
Integration tests for sandbox blocking
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: exec was already in jacl_non_core_builtins. Added exec availability check at compile time. Custom exec closures trigger OP_GET_GLOBAL + OP_CALL path instead of OP_EXEC. 7 integration tests added.

userStories.title: Argument handling — literals and splat
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want predictable argument handling with explicit glob support.
acceptanceCriteria: `!ls *.txt` passes literal `"*.txt"` to ls (no expansion)
`!ls ..[glob "*.txt"]` splats glob results as separate args
`!cmd $arg` passes variable value as single arg
`!cmd ..$args` splats vector elements as separate args
Empty splat `..[]` adds no args
Args with spaces work: `!cmd "hello world"` is single arg
Integration tests for various arg patterns
build.sh passes
userStories.notes: Spread support implemented using OP_VEC_SPREAD. Literals pass through unchanged (no shell expansion). Note: glob builtin not implemented; tested with vector spread (..[vec ...]) and ..[expr] syntax. 7 integration tests added.
